sentences.text: The name Melanorosaurus translates to "Black Mountain Lizard," combining Greek roots for black, mountain, and lizard.
This large herbivore from South Africa possessed a massive body and sturdy limbs, indicating it moved on all fours.
The skull of this animal measured approximately 250 millimeters in length.
Its premaxilla bone featured four teeth on each side, a trait typical of primitive sauropodomorphs.
Like many sauropod vertebrae, the bones of Melanorosaurus contained hollow spaces to reduce overall weight.
The creature reached a length of 8 meters and a mass of 1.3 metric tons.
Its limb bones were notably massive and heavy, resembling those of true sauropods.
Sidney H. Haughton originally described and named the genus in 1924.
A 2024 review designated specimen SAM-PK-3449 as the lectotype.
The first complete skull, cataloged as NM QR3314, was not described until 2007.
Recent research moved several bones, including a femur, to the new combination Meroktenos thabanensis.
While formerly placed in prosauropods, Melanorosaurus is now viewed as one of the earliest sauropods.
Basal forms like this animal serve as intermediates between prosauropods and true sauropods.
Depending on the definition used, it may be classified as an early sauropod.
Adam Yates proposed a definition that excludes Melanorosaurus from Sauropoda.
Although prosauropods were once thought to be ancestors, ankle bone designs suggest they are sister groups.
Melanorosaurus readi lived during the Late Triassic, roughly 210 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
The time range for the genus spans from the Norian to the Sinemurian, approximately 227.3 to 192.9 million years ago.
Fossils were found in the Lower Elliot Formation on the north slope of the Black Mountain in Transkei.
